description: Utility and developer orders, transformer configuration and pricing, quotes, order changes, and storm-restoration orders in the ERP
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Orders can be taken on paper for 2 days; storm-restoration orders must be confirmed within 24 hours under utility agreements; order changes lost after the RPO cause wrong builds
manual_workaround: Paper order forms and the printed price book; storm orders confirmed by phone and email by the storm desk; back-entry after recovery
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; ERP software vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Sales and customer service (about 380); storm desk
quantified_impact_basis: Rework, overtime, and delayed bookings; revenue is deferred, not lost, for the first 2 days
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 quotes in its legacy ERP

description: Finite-capacity schedule for P1 to P6, material requirements planning, capacity reservations for storm units, and daily schedule publication to the MES
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Plants run from the last printed 5-day schedule for about 2 days, then sequencing errors and material shortages compound; storm-season reservations must be honored; schedule changes after the RPO are hard to reconstruct
manual_workaround: Printed 5-day schedules refreshed daily; spreadsheet sequencing by plant planners; daily planning call across plants
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; ERP software vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: Central planning team (about 60) and plant planners
quantified_impact_basis: After day 2, about 20% of P1 to P5 shipments ($16.7 million per production day across all plants) slip because of sequencing and material errors
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 schedules in its legacy ERP (BP-17)
single_points_of_failure: Single APS instance; schedule logic held by 4 senior planners

business_process: Work order release and shop-floor execution (MES)
description: Work order release from the ERP to the MES at P1 to P6, electronic travelers, labor and material confirmations, and quality holds (about 46,000 work orders a month)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Paper travelers sustain about one shift; after 24 hours untraceable work and quality holds stop shipments; confirmations lost after the RPO break traceability for test reports
manual_workaround: Printed travelers and paper confirmation sheets kept at each line; supervisors hold release of untraceable units
dependent_third_parties: MES software vendor; Cloud provider A
quantified_impact_basis: About half of P1 to P6 daily shipments deferred once paper travelers run out after one shift
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 uses its own legacy MES (BP-17)
single_points_of_failure: One MES application tier per plant

description: Core and coil assembly, tanking, oil fill, routine test, and paint for pad-mounted and pole-mounted units
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Storm-restoration demand: utilities need units within days after a hurricane; MTD falls to 24 hours when a storm watch covers a customer service area; controller programs change rarely, so the RPO is the last nightly program backup
manual_workaround: Local PLCs keep running if HMIs fail; manual recipe entry from printed winding sheets with engineering double-check; units without certified test data held
dependent_third_parties: OEMs of winding and core cutting machines; grain-oriented electrical steel and copper suppliers
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 3,600 workers at P1 and P3
quantified_impact_basis: P1 ($4.6 million) and P3 ($3.4 million) shipments per production day
single_points_of_failure: Two plants make all single-phase pole-mounted units (P3)

business_process: Power transformer production (P2, P4, and P5)
description: Core stacking, winding, vapor-phase drying, vacuum oil processing, tanking, and final assembly of power and large power transformers
process_owner: Plant Managers, P2, P4, and P5
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Safety sets the RTO: drying ovens and vacuum oil systems must be monitored from an HMI or held in a safe state; an interrupted drying cycle may have to restart (2 to 5 days lost); liquidated damages accrue on late units
manual_workaround: Local PLC operation under operator watch at the panel; oven safe-state procedures; no new drying cycle without HMI supervision
dependent_third_parties: Drying oven and vacuum system OEMs; bushing and tap changer suppliers
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 3,900 workers at P2, P4, and P5
quantified_impact_basis: P2 ($3.9 million), P4 ($2.0 million), and P5 ($2.0 million) shipments per production day; liquidated damages of 0.5% of contract value per week on late units are extra
single_points_of_failure: P2 is the only plant that builds units above 345 kV

description: Core steel slitting, cut cores, preformed windings, and tanks shipped to the other plants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Other plants hold about 5 production days of P6 parts; after that BP-04 and BP-05 stop
manual_workaround: Buy cut cores from an outside supplier for distribution units; expedite tanks
quantified_impact_basis: Expediting and outside purchase premium while buffers last

business_process: Testing, certified test reports, and DOE certification data
description: Routine and type tests at every plant, high-voltage tests at P2, P4, and P5, certified test reports, and DOE certification test records in the TDMS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No unit ships without a certified test report; test data must be retained for DOE review (10 CFR 429.71); loss of raw test data forces retesting
manual_workaround: Test stations store results locally for 30 days; printed test sheets signed by Quality; retest where data integrity is in doubt
dependent_people_or_facilities: Test technicians and quality engineers; P2 extra-high-voltage laboratory
quantified_impact_basis: After 72 hours, finished units awaiting reports (about 15% of daily shipments) are held
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 test data on a legacy file server (no index or backup)
single_points_of_failure: P2 laboratory is the only extra-high-voltage test lab

description: Electromagnetic and mechanical design, drawings, winding specifications, and customer drawing exchange in the PLM and the engineering compute cluster
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Released designs are already in the ERP and MES; new designs slip after a week; loss of unreleased design work is costly
manual_workaround: Released drawings cached on plant engineering file shares; design reviews postponed
dependent_systems: SYS-03 (PLM on Cloud provider A; compute cluster at DC-1)
quantified_impact_basis: Idle engineering time and later delivery of new designs
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 designs on a separate CAD vault
single_points_of_failure: Engineering compute cluster in DC-1 only

description: Purchase orders, supplier schedules, and advance ship notices for grain-oriented electrical steel, copper, insulating fluids, bushings, tap changers, and TMU electronics (about 3,400 EDI documents a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Supplier schedules cover about 3 days; long-lead steel and bushings slip if releases stop
manual_workaround: Email purchase orders from a printed open-order report; supplier portal downloads
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 purchases through its legacy ERP

business_process: Shipping, heavy-haul logistics, and export screening
description: Shipping documents, heavy-haul and rail permits for large power transformers, restricted-party screening, and export records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Export orders must not ship without screening; heavy-haul moves are booked weeks ahead and are expensive to rebook; EAR records must be kept 5 years (15 CFR 762.6)
manual_workaround: Domestic shipments with manual bills of lading; no export shipment without a documented manual screening by Trade Compliance
dependent_third_parties: Heavy-haul carriers and railroads; restricted-party screening data service
quantified_impact_basis: Finished units held in yards (about 12% of daily shipments) plus rebooking fees
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 ships from its legacy ERP
single_points_of_failure: Screening service integrated only with the ERP

business_process: Field service, commissioning, and storm response
description: Commissioning, repairs, TMU setup at utility sites, and storm crews (about 900 staff, 9 service centers)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Utilities depend on storm crews within a day of landfall; access-revocation notices are due within 1 business day under the addenda
manual_workaround: Printed crew rosters and job packets; dispatch by phone
quantified_impact_basis: Field service and repair revenue per day; storm penalties under some agreements
single_points_of_failure: Field laptops hold utility-specific configuration tools

description: Ingestion of utility TMU data, condition analytics (AI-003), advisories, and the customer portal for about 60 subscribers and 14,500 transformers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Subscription agreements: 99.5% monthly portal availability and advisories within 24 hours of a high-severity alert; utilities buffer data for 72 hours on their side
manual_workaround: Reliability engineers call subscribers about known high-risk units; utilities keep their own alarms
quantified_impact_basis: Daily subscription revenue ($0.26 million) plus service credits and renewal risk

description: Member reservations, emergency dispatch decisions, and allocation of 64 spare large power and generator step-up transformers held in 3 yards
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Member agreements: dispatch decision within 24 hours of a qualifying emergency request; allocation records must be accurate
manual_workaround: Printed spare registry (refreshed weekly) and phone dispatch by the spares desk; not yet tested (POAM-024)
quantified_impact_basis: Daily member fees ($0.4 million); a missed dispatch also delays a member utility restoring service

business_process: TMU firmware release and product security response
description: Firmware and configuration software builds, signing, SBOMs, the download portal, PSIRT intake, and vulnerability disclosure to utilities
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Addenda: vulnerability disclosure within 30 days and hashes for every release; an emergency fix for an exploited flaw must ship within days
manual_workaround: Freeze releases; publish hashes and advisories through the security contacts in the obligations register
dependent_third_parties: Code repository SaaS; cloud hardware security module; TMU electronics contract manufacturer
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering idle time; the main exposure is contractual and reputational
single_points_of_failure: Signing key in one hardware security module cluster

description: Weekly production payroll and biweekly salaried payroll for 12,000 employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Weekly production payroll; wage payment laws in each state
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll and true up later
dependent_systems: SYS-13 (HR and payroll SaaS); SYS-05 (time capture)
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 payroll moved to the enterprise provider in 2025-10

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual SEC filings, and SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; during the quarter-end window the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Close from the last ERP extract; delay the earnings release only as a last resort
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime; the main exposure is regulatory
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 ledger consolidated monthly by journal upload

business_process: AQ-01 (P7) operations on legacy ERP and MES
description: Orders, schedules, work orders, and test records for dry-type and specialty transformers at the Ohio plant
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Data center customers hold delivery penalties; legacy systems back up nightly only, so the real RPO is 24 hours against a 1-hour target
dependent_systems: AQ-01 legacy ERP and MES; AQ-01 OT; legacy directory
dependent_third_parties: Legacy ERP vendor (limited support); OEMs on cellular routers
single_points_of_failure: Single on-premises server room; restore never tested

description: Incident notices to the 88 addendum utilities, access-revocation notices, federal contracting officer reports, SEC disclosure support, and breach notices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The shortest clocks: 24-hour incident notice in 27 addenda, 1 business day for FAR 52.204-25(d) and access-revocation notices, 4 business days for Form 8-K Item 1.05 after a materiality determination
manual_workaround: Printed obligations register and utility security contact list in the incident binders; notices sent from out-of-band email accounts
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time; the exposure is breach of contract and disclosure risk
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 customer contracts not yet in the obligations register (12 addenda)
